title: Plumbline standing constitution
description: The standing frame for a program: values, core principles, and the buyer/specialist provenance that loans the evaluator its authority (Contracts s1.1, s4). Ratified ONCE per program and versioned, then referenced by every job packet. Per-job framing (job-to-be-done, pain points, desired future, ground truth, thresholds) does NOT live here — it belongs to the job packet. The split exists to remove repeated burden: a standard agreed once should not be re-specified every job, and a re-specified standard is one that will drift.

program.description: The program this constitution governs. One constitution per program, not per job.

version.description: Semantic version. A job packet records the version it was written under, so a later reader can tell which standard a decision was judged against.

ratified.description: False while any value below is `proposed, unratified`. While false, no job under this constitution can reach the `accepted` terminal state (s3).

ratified_by.description: Who agreed this standard. Recorded, not implied.

values.description: Ranked, if rank matters. Each value carries a decision rule; see the value definition.

provenance.description: Where this principle comes from. A principle with no provenance is a preference.

applies_to_stages.description: Restrict a principle to the stages it governs. Omit to apply everywhere.

escalation_classes.description: Standing escalation classes that bypass regeneration and go straight to a human. Values and doctrine questions always belong here (s2, s4). Per-job classes are added by the packet, never subtracted from this list.

human_seat.description: Standing delivery target for escalations. In this workspace a queue (e.g. a Telegram topic), never a blocking prompt in a headless run.

non_negotiable.description: Things that are never delegated to any agent at any stage, regardless of confidence or cost.

proposed.description: The single permitted home for unratified standing values (s3). Nowhere else.

provenance.description: s1.1: a rubric that cannot answer 'who is buying this, and which master of the craft approved the standard?' is invalid.

decision_rule.description: REQUIRED. What this value forces when two defensible options conflict. A value with no decision rule cannot arbitrate and therefore cannot be applied by an evaluator or an orchestrator — it is decoration, and it will be resolved by whoever is loudest. Stating the rule is what converts a value into something mechanical (s1.1, s4: the evaluator's authority is on loan from the buyer, and a loan needs terms).

rank.description: Optional. Set when values can conflict and must resolve in a fixed order.

evidence_of_adherence.description: Optional. How adherence to this value could be observed rather than asserted.
